title: NetworkError and stricter retries
summary: Ky now wraps a recognized fetch network failure in a typed NetworkError. By default it retries only errors it knows and throws every other error at once.

steps.title: Fetch errors are vague
steps.body:
- When a request fails at the network level, `fetch` rejects with a plain `TypeError`.
- Each runtime words this error differently. Chrome says "Failed to fetch". Firefox says "NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.". Node.js says "fetch failed". Safari 17 and later say "Load failed".
- A programming bug can throw a `TypeError` too, such as "Cannot read properties of undefined".
- So the error type alone does not show a network failure. Only the message can show it.

steps.title: Ky retried every error
steps.body:
- Before this PR, `#calculateRetryDelay` decided about retries. It had rules for two error types only: `TimeoutError` and `HTTPError`.
- Any other error on a retriable method reached the last line, which returned a delay. So Ky retried that error up to the retry limit.
- A network failure and a bug in a custom `fetch` got the same retries.
- Issue #545 asked how to retry only real network errors. In that issue, sholladay confirmed that Ky retried all fetch errors, "whether they are network errors or not".
- The workaround in the issue was a `beforeRetry` hook that throws any error that is not a network error.

links.title: Issue #545: Best way to handle Fetch errors

steps.title: The decision
steps.body:
sholladay proposed this plan in #545. sindresorhus called the retry part "the most pragmatic solution".
- `#fetch` wraps a recognized network error in a new `NetworkError`. sholladay wanted this "to normalize them and make it more obvious what's going on".
- `#calculateRetryDelay` retries only the error types Ky knows: `NetworkError`, `HTTPError` with a retriable status, and `TimeoutError` when `retryOnTimeout` is set. It throws any other error at once.
- The cost: Ky no longer retries a network error with a message it does not know, such as one from a new runtime. sholladay preferred retries in that case.
- sindresorhus accepted the cost: "New runtimes don't come along every day."
- `shouldRetry` covers the gap. It runs before the error-type checks. The readme now points users to it for errors that Ky does not recognize.

steps.title: Why the detector is inlined
steps.body:
- Ky must recognize a network failure by its message. The package `is-network-error` already does that.
- The PR copies `is-network-error` v1.3.1 into `source/utils/is-network-error.ts`. It does not add the package as a dependency.
- The copy has the name `isRawNetworkError`, so it does not clash with the new public guard `isNetworkError`.
- sholladay found inlining "a bit silly", because Ky already has a compile step.
- sindresorhus replied that a compile step for a dependency is "not worth the effort for a single one that won't update very often."

steps.title: Errors from fetch
steps.say: A network failure first reaches Ky as a raw error from `fetch`.

terms.meaning: A `TypeError` from `fetch` with a message that a runtime uses for a network failure, such as "Failed to fetch". `isRawNetworkError`, the inlined copy of `is-network-error` v1.3.1, detects it.
The set of exact messages that `isRawNetworkError` looks up, with a comment that names the runtime of each. A few messages, such as "Failed to fetch", have their own checks before this lookup.

steps.title: Ky's error types
steps.say: `#fetch` now turns a raw network error into one of Ky's own error types.

terms.meaning: The base class of all Ky errors. `HTTPError`, `NetworkError`, `TimeoutError` and `ForceRetryError` extend it.
The new `KyError` that `#fetch` throws for a raw network error. It has `request`, and its message names the method and the URL.
The standard `Error` property that holds the error behind this one. A `NetworkError` keeps the raw `TypeError` in `cause`.
The new public type guard for a `NetworkError`. It is true for an instance of `NetworkError` or for any error whose `name` is `'NetworkError'`.
The `KyError` that Ky throws for a response with a non-2xx status when `throwHttpErrors` is on. It has `response` and `request`.
The `KyError` that Ky throws when the request times out. Ky retries it only when the `retryOnTimeout` option is `true`.

steps.title: The retry decision
steps.say: After an attempt fails with one of these errors, the retry decision chooses a retry or a throw.

terms.meaning: The private method `Ky#calculateRetryDelay`. After a failed attempt, it returns a delay in ms to retry, or it throws the error to stop.
The most retries after the first attempt. The default is 2, so a request makes at most 3 attempts.
An HTTP method in `retry.methods`. The defaults are GET, PUT, HEAD, DELETE, OPTIONS and TRACE, so Ky does not retry a POST.

An optional user function that the retry decision calls after the limit and method checks. It returns `true` to force a retry, `false` to stop, or `undefined` to leave the choice to the error-type checks.
A user hook that runs before each retry and gets the error. For a network failure, that error is now a `NetworkError`.
A user hook that can change an error right before Ky throws it to the caller. For a network failure, it now gets a `NetworkError`.

steps.title: Which errors retry now
steps.say: An attempt failed. Which errors does Ky retry now?

notes.text: An attempt failed. `#retry` passes the error to `#calculateRetryDelay`. This method returns a delay to retry, or it throws the error.

Three unchanged checks run first. Ky throws at the retry limit, or when `retry.methods` does not include the method. When set, `shouldRetry` forces a retry with `true`, throws with `false`, and hands the error on with `undefined`.
A `TimeoutError` retries only when `retryOnTimeout` is `true`. The default is `false`, so a timeout throws.
An `HTTPError` retries when `retry.statusCodes` includes its status. Any other status throws.
A `NetworkError` now retries. `#fetch` throws this error when fetch fails with a known runtime message.

Any other error now throws at once, such as a `TypeError` from a bug in a custom `fetch`. Before, the last line of `#calculateRetryDelay` returned a delay. So Ky retried every error that reached that line.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: With a retry limit of 2, how many attempts does a GET make when fetch fails with a non-network `TypeError` and `shouldRetry` returns `undefined`?

options.why: `undefined` hands the error to the error type checks, and the last check throws any error that is not a `NetworkError`.

options.text: 3, because only `false` from `shouldRetry` stops a retry.
options.why: `undefined` does not force a retry, so the error type checks still throw the `TypeError`.
The method check only lets the error go on, and the error type checks then throw the `TypeError`.

options.text: 2, because the retry limit counts the first attempt.
options.why: The limit counts retries, and here the error type checks throw before the first retry.

steps.title: Wrap and retry a failed fetch
steps.say: The first fetch of `ky.get(url)` fails with a network `TypeError`. `Ky#fetch` now wraps the error in a `NetworkError`. The retry decision retries it because it is a `NetworkError`.

steps.title: Both send paths reach the catch
steps.say: `#fetch` now wraps both send paths in one `try` block. Each path awaits its promise, so a rejection reaches the `catch`.

notes.text: Before, `#fetch` had no `try` block. It returned each send promise as it was, so a rejection went straight to `#retry`.
The `try` now covers the `timeout: false` path too. That path calls `options.fetch` directly, so it needs its own `return await`.
With the timeout turned off, the test still gets a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` in `cause`.
The `timeout()` path also awaits its promise. A bare `return` in an async function hands the promise to the caller, so its rejection would skip the `catch`.

steps.title: The catch spots raw network errors
steps.say: The `catch` asks `isRawNetworkError` whether the error is a raw network error. The check reads only the error name and message, because the runtimes give no shared error code.

notes.text: The `catch` calls `isRawNetworkError` on every error from the send. The name keeps it apart from the public `isNetworkError` guard. That guard checks for a `NetworkError` instead.
A message without its own rule must match an entry in the list exactly. The rules above this line match Chrome's `Failed to fetch`, Safari's `Load failed`, and Deno's message.

`errorMessages` holds the network error messages of Chrome, Firefox, Safari 16, Node.js, Bun, Cloudflare Workers, and `cross-fetch`. The file is a copy of `is-network-error` v1.3.1, inlined so Ky adds no dependency.

steps.title: A fetch failure becomes a NetworkError
steps.say: A raw network error leaves `#fetch` as a `NetworkError`, with the raw error in `cause`. Every other error leaves `#fetch` as it was.

notes.text: A raw network error becomes a `NetworkError` for `this.request`, with the raw `TypeError` as `cause`. `#fetch` rethrows any other error as it is. Examples are a `TypeError` with another message and a `TimeoutError` from the timer or the spent budget.
`NetworkError` extends `KyError`, the base class of Ky's errors. Its `name` is `'NetworkError'`. `request` holds the request that failed.
The message ends with the method and the URL, such as `GET https://example.com/`. The constructor passes `options` on to `Error`, so `cause` is the standard `Error.cause`.
In Node.js, the `code` from undici now sits one level deeper, at `error.cause.cause.code`. Code that reads `error.cause.code` no longer finds it.

steps.title: Only known error types retry
steps.say: The checks for the retry limit, the retriable method, and `shouldRetry` still run first. After them, only a `TimeoutError`, an `HTTPError`, or a `NetworkError` can get a delay. Every other error now throws.

notes.text: Before, a `TimeoutError` with `retryOnTimeout` set fell through to the shared return at the end.
The timeout branch now returns its own delay. Without this `return`, a `TimeoutError` would reach the new tail and throw.
A retriable `HTTPError` that reaches this line now returns its backoff delay here. Before, it also fell through to the shared return.
Before, the shared return gave a delay to every error that reached it. That included programming bugs, such as a `TypeError` from a custom `fetch`.
Now only a `NetworkError` gets the delay. Any other error throws, so Ky makes no further attempt.
`isNetworkError` checks `instanceof`, or the `name` for an error from another realm. The other Ky guards use the same pattern.
`isKyError` now also accepts an error that passes `isNetworkError`. A `NetworkError` from another realm now counts as a `KyError` too.
A custom `fetch` throws `TypeError('Cannot read properties of undefined')` with a retry limit of 2. `fetch` runs once. The caller gets the raw `TypeError`.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: What happens when a GET with a retry limit of 2 and no `shouldRetry` uses a custom `fetch` that always rejects with `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`?

options.text: `fetch` runs 3 times, and the caller catches a `NetworkError` with the `TypeError` in `cause`.
options.why: `Failed to fetch` is a known message, so each failure is a `NetworkError` that retries until the limit of 2 stops it.

options.text: `fetch` runs once, and the caller catches the raw `TypeError`.
options.why: Only an unknown message stops after one call, and `Failed to fetch` is a known message.

options.text: `fetch` runs 3 times, and the caller catches the raw `TypeError`.
options.why: `#fetch` wraps every recognized failure, so the raw `TypeError` is only in `cause`.

options.text: `fetch` runs once, and the caller catches a `NetworkError`.
options.why: GET is a retriable method, so a `NetworkError` gets a delay and Ky retries it twice.

steps.title: A non-network TypeError fails at once
steps.say: A bug in a custom `fetch` rejects with a `TypeError` whose message matches no rule. Before, Ky retried it like a network failure. Now the app gets the raw `TypeError` after one attempt.

messages.note: The error keeps its type and its message.

messages.note: After the `beforeError` hooks run, the app gets the raw `TypeError` from one fetch call.

steps.title: A POST throws NetworkError at once
steps.say: A POST is not a retriable method, so its first `NetworkError` is final. The method check is unchanged. The app now gets a `NetworkError` instead of the raw `TypeError`.

messages.label: throw NetworkError
messages.note: `#fetch` wraps the network failure of the first attempt.

messages.label: #calculateRetryDelay(error)
messages.note: The retry limit check passes on the first attempt.

messages.label: throw, POST not retriable
messages.note: The method check runs before any error type check, so `post` stops here.

messages.label: error leaves #retry
messages.note: The `NetworkError` rejects the `await` in the request lifecycle.

messages.label: beforeError({error})
messages.note: Each `beforeError` hook now gets the `NetworkError`.

messages.label: error
messages.note: A hook that returns an `Error` replaces the error, and any other value keeps it.

steps.title: What to check before merge
steps.body:
- Retries now depend on the detector. Before, the default logic retried any error it did not know. Now an error that is not a `TimeoutError` or an `HTTPError` retries only as a `NetworkError`.
- The detector misses some real network failures: node-fetch's `FetchError` (its name is not `TypeError`), Safari `Load failed` with a stack, and runtime messages that change later. These failures lose their retries. Only a readme caveat and `shouldRetry` cover them. Nothing syncs the inlined v1.3.1 copy with upstream.
- The wrap covers only the send in `#fetch`. undici may throw `terminated` later, while `.json()` reads the body. That error stays a raw `TypeError`, and Ky does not retry it. The readme says that network errors are retried.
- undici's `fetch failed` is generic. undici also uses it for client-side mistakes. The tests show two: an `invalid:` URL and a `content-length` mismatch. These now become a `NetworkError`, so Ky retries them on a retriable method such as GET.
- Callers that read the raw error break. Checks on `instanceof TypeError`, `error.message` or `error.cause.code` now see a `NetworkError`. The raw error sits one level deeper, in `cause`.
- The workaround from #545 now stops retries. Its `beforeRetry` hook throws unless the `is-network-error` package matches the error. The package needs the name `TypeError`, so every `NetworkError` fails. The v2.0.0-0 release notes list this PR under "New", not under "Breaking".
- `isNetworkError` also matches by `name`. Any error named `NetworkError` passes, such as a `DOMException` with that name. `#calculateRetryDelay` retries such an error. The guard types it as having `request`, but it has none.

steps.title: Also changed
steps.body:
- `source/core/Ky.ts`: new imports.
- `source/index.ts`: exports `NetworkError` and `isNetworkError`.
- `source/errors/KyError.ts`: the doc comment lists `NetworkError` as a subclass.
- `source/errors/HTTPError.ts`: the doc comment now names the `options` property. This edit is not about network errors.
- `source/types/hooks.ts`: the `beforeRetry` and `beforeError` docs now name `NetworkError`.
- `source/types/options.ts`: the `retry` doc lists every retry field and adds a paragraph on network retries. It fixes the `maxRetryAfter` wording. It drops the stale line "Retries are not triggered following a timeout".
- `source/types/retry.ts`: the `maxRetryAfter` doc now says it caps the wait. Before, it said the request is canceled. The `shouldRetry` doc says that `undefined` does not retry unknown errors.
- `readme.md`: mirrors the JSDoc and adds a `NetworkError` section with a caveat about runtime heuristics.
- `test/hooks.ts`: fake fetch failures now throw `TypeError('Failed to fetch')`, so they still retry. Checks for a raw `TypeError` now use `isNetworkError`.
- `test/memory-leak.ts`: expects a `NetworkError` instead of `TypeError('fetch failed')`.
- `test/retry.ts`: new imports of `NetworkError`, `isKyError` and `isNetworkError`.

steps.title: Other tests
steps.body:
`test/retry.ts` also pins these behaviors:
- A `TypeError('Failed to fetch')` becomes a `NetworkError` with `request`, `cause` and the message `Request failed due to a network error: GET https://example.com/`.
- Two `Failed to fetch` failures and then a `Response` resolve to `ok` after 3 calls.
- A POST makes 1 call and rejects with a `NetworkError`.
- `shouldRetry` and a `beforeError` hook both get the `NetworkError`, with the `TypeError` in `cause`.
- When `shouldRetry` returns `undefined`, the default retry still runs.
- When `shouldRetry` returns `true`, Ky retries a non-network `TypeError` up to the limit.

steps.title: Where to read next
steps.body:
- `#calculateRetryDelay` in `source/core/Ky.ts`: the whole retry decision, with `ForceRetryError` and the `Retry-After` headers.
- `source/utils/is-network-error.ts`: the runtime rules this dive left out. They cover Safari `Load failed`, the Deno message prefix and Chrome's `Failed to fetch (host)` form.
- The `NetworkError` section of `readme.md`: the public docs and the caveat about runtime heuristics.
